selected.title: Robotic Inguinal vs Transabdominal Laparoscopic Inguinal Hernia Repair: The RIVAL Randomized Clinical Trial.
selected.why: First multicentre RCT (n=102, rTAPP vs lTAPP): no difference in pain/QoL/wound events at 30 d; longer OR time (75.5 vs 40.5 min), higher cost ($3258 vs $1421), more surgeon frustration.

selected.title: Laparoscopic versus robotic inguinal hernia repair: 1- and 2-year outcomes from the RIVAL trial.
selected.why: Only RCT long-term data: pain, QoL (SF-36), physical activity and recurrence (1 vs 1) similar at 1-2 years; ~25% loss to follow-up.

selected.title: Robotic versus laparoscopic minimally invasive inguinal hernia repair: randomized clinical trial (the ROGER trial).
selected.why: Largest blinded RCT vs TEP (n=182, rTAPP vs lTEP): no difference in 24-h pain or complications; rTAPP 16 min longer; lower surgeon workload (NASA-TLX).

selected.title: Shorter operative times following robotic-assisted transabdominal preperitoneal inguinal hernia repair (TAPP) compared to laparoscopic TAPP: the Danish Inguinal Randomized Controlled Trial (DIRECT).
selected.why: RCT (n=138) by experienced surgeons: rTAPP had SHORTER operative time than lTAPP despite ~5 min docking; key for operative-time question.

selected.title: Inflammatory response and short-term outcomes after laparoscopic versus robotic transabdominal preperitoneal inguinal hernia repair: randomized clinical trial (ROLAIS).
selected.why: Open-label RCT (n=139): rTAPP lower CRP/IL-6, shorter OR time (-13.4 min), fewer complications (23% vs 41.5%), more same-day discharge; no chronic pain/recurrence difference.

selected.title: Robotic assisted surgery reduces ergonomic risk during minimally invasive inguinal hernia repair: the VOLTAIRE randomised controlled trial.
selected.why: RCT (n=59, open-console robot): better surgeon ergonomics, more patients back to normal activity at 14 d (39% vs 5%), but OR time doubled (65 vs 32 min).

selected.title: Laparoscopic versus robotic transabdominal preperitoneal inguinal hernia repair: a randomized controlled trial.
selected.why: Newest RCT, Indian (AIIMS) setting (n=101, 2:1, double-blind): no difference in early pain, OR time, return to activity or 4-week complications; questions value in low-resource settings.

selected.title: Stray energy injury during robotic versus laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair: a randomized controlled trial.
selected.why: Small VA RCT of rTAPP vs lTAPP on a safety mechanism: port-site stray thermal injury similar (60% vs 49%); included for completeness of RCT set.

selected.title: Robotic versus laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
selected.why: Most comprehensive RCT-only MA (7 RCTs, 9 reports, 691 pts, TAPP+TEP comparators, GRADE): no significant difference in any outcome incl. complications, recurrence, same-day discharge, QoL, cost; low/very-low certainty.

selected.title: Robotic Versus Laparoscopic Transabdominal Preperitoneal Inguinal Hernia Repair: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
selected.journal: J Laparoendosc Adv Surg Tech A
selected.why: Most recent RCT-only MA (search to Aug 2026; 4 rTAPP vs lTAPP RCTs, 401 pts, RoB2/GRADE): no difference in complications, seroma, hematoma, SSI; OR time +18.5 min NS with I2 98%.

possible_contradictions.note: ROLAIS found robotic TAPP BETTER: fewer complications (23% vs 41.5%), fewer haematomas, shorter OR time, more same-day discharge, lower inflammatory markers. Open-label, single centre; lap arm complication rate unusually high.

DIRECT found robotic TAPP FASTER than laparoscopic TAPP, opposite to RIVAL, ROGER and VOLTAIRE, which all found robotic longer. Experienced surgeons; operative time drives the high heterogeneity (I2 ~98%) in the MAs.
VOLTAIRE: more robotic patients back to normal activity at 14 d (39% vs 5%), a secondary outcome in a small RCT; the AIIMS RCT 42527734 found no difference in return to activity.
Mixed-design MA reports lower recurrence with robotic repair (RR 0.32), unlike RCT-only MAs (RD 0.00); driven by observational cohorts, low certainty.
Mixed-design MA rTAPP vs lTEP with TSA claims robust reduction in postoperative pain (MD -1.59), whereas the ROGER RCT (same comparison) found no pain difference.
